title: Stop Trying: Effortless Action and Belief
one_liner: Perceived difficulty is mimetic — stop trying hard and let belief replace effortful thinking.
caption: If you try, you won’t. Cool guy doesn’t rush. Being chill never broke a sweat. Just because it was hard for your father, doesn’t mean it has to be hard for you.

There's a panda who was raised by humans, and she grimaces every time she breaks bamboo because that's what she saw her human caretakers do. Naturally, pandas are strong enough to break this no problem. She does this solely as a product of imitation, and this really lends towards Girard's mimetic theory that humans naturally don't really know how to do anything or what to want, and that we imitate desires and we imitate actions. And we learn this from mediators, and it's the prestigious mediators that modify how we view an object. So for example, this panda sees humans wincing when they break bamboo, and now all of a sudden the bamboo becomes harder to break. This is because the brain creates forward models and practices predictive processing and motor control. You see this in the size-weight illusion, where the brain miscalculates motor output for different sized objects, even though the person knows that the weight is the same. In this case, when a task becomes harder, it's the opposite of placebo, it's nocebo. The weight is perceived heavier. The situation more difficult. Rather than pro-noy, one experiences paranoia. They think everybody's out to get them. Everything becomes harder. And this is not new. Epictetus says it. Marcus Aurelius says it. Seneca says it. But my favorite is Menander. You've suffered nothing terrible unless you pretend that you have. You have to pretend to suffer. A man is only as miserable as he thinks he is. Nothing is good or bad, but thinking makes it so. So think right. Of course, this is the concept of like wu-wei and Taoism. This is effortless action. To be in harmony with nature, to be a natural. Nature never rushes, yet everything is accomplished. Nature doesn't sweat it. Nature doesn't try hard, it just does. Do or do not, there is no try, says Yoda. Why? Because through mimesis, Luke has created these schemas in his mind that keep him from using the force. So when the child tries to get Neo to bend the spoon, he can't do it. Neo's mind is clouded with thoughts of metallurgy and his mind tells him, this is a spoon, this is a spoon, this is a spoon. And so you ask the kid, how do you bend the spoon? The child simply says, there is no spoon. He's beginning to believe Morpheus says later. Belief is not the attainment of new information, it's the forgetting of concepts. It's the annihilation of the idea of the spoon. It's forgetting the hardness of the bamboo. Removing opinion and prejudice and personality. Because I agree with Schopenhauer. The individual intellect interferes with the will, the instinct. Will is limbic and existed before the frontal lobe. The intellect serves the will, all is will. But the material world gets in the way. Rationality and desire gets in the way. The idea of the X-wing and the spoon and the bamboo. That is why the first statement of the Lord's Prayer, after addressing the Father is, thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Or as Jesus says in Gethsemane, your will, not mine. It's the stripping of intellect and personality in favor of the universal, the force. And when you believe, it doesn't require effort. There's a story of the centurion asks for Jesus to heal his servant. And Jesus says, yeah, do you want me to walk over there? And the centurion is like, no, I'm your servant, just say it and it'll be done. And Jesus says, he displays the most belief out of all the people in Israel. He doesn't need Jesus to make an effort. He believes, it's as simple as that. Faith and belief confound the minds of scientists. They have to call it spooky action in the distance. Stop trying so hard, stop scheming and plotting. Roadrunner never tries, it always goes unharmed. While Wile E. Coyote devises clever and cleverer plans that always explode in his face. Silly rabbit, tricks are for kids. The deceptive rabbit doesn't realize that he just needs to become childlike. There's nothing to do. There's no disguise he can wear, no plan he can come up with. Unless you become like a child, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven. You must become a child again. The child knows no names and concepts. He knows that there is no spoon. Childlike innocence always beats devious scheming. Being present requires a permanent state of selectively optimistic amnesia. Don't try it, just do it. Every kid understands this. Luke, Neo, Roadrunner, Jesus Christ. Don't try, silly panda. There is no bamboo.

author: Marina Lydia Georgallides
title: Greek Lamb Chops (Paidakia) Recipe
one_liner: Juicy Greek-style grilled lamb chops marinated in olive oil, lemon, garlic, and oregano.
caption:
Ep 102 of EAT LIKE A GREEK🇬🇷✨PAIDAKIA😮‍💨 follow @chefmarinie for more easy Greek recipes! 

If there’s one thing Greeks know how to do… it’s lamb 😮‍💨and these lamb chops right here are hands down the juiciest ones you’ll ever eat 👏🏻

📌RECIPE BELOW - 8 lamb chops - serves 2-3

Gather 
8 lamb chops 

For the marinade 
50ml extra virgin Greek olive oil 
1 lemon, juiced 
3 garlic cloves, grated 
2 tbsp dried oregano 
1 tsp dried thyme 
1 1/2 tsp pink Himalayan sea salt 
1/2 tsp ground black pepper 

Method 
1.) Prepare the marinade by mixing all the ingredients together in a jug. 
2.) In a large mixing bowl, place the lamb chops and coat them in the marinade. Mix to combine well and cover and refrigerate for at least two hours to let the flavours marinate. 
3.) Let the lamb rest out of the fridge for 20-30 minutes, depending on how warm your kitchen is. This process allows the lamb to develop a crispy edge. 
4.) Heat up a griddle pan over a medium to high heat. After 3-4 minutes, place each lamb chop, leaving a little gap between each one. Cook for 4 minutes on both sides, and 30 seconds on the fat side down. 
5.) Place the cooked lamb chops on a plate and leave to rest for at least 5 minutes. Meanwhile, pour the raw marinade into a saucepan with a few splashes of water.  Let it bubble briskly for 3-4 minutes on a high heat, stirring, until it’s simmered well throughout. This cooks off any bacteria that may have come from the raw lamb. 
6.) Pour the cooked sauce over the lamb chops and serve with a wedge of lemon. I recommend serving with tzatziki and a potato salad. 

#lamb #easyrecipe #greekfood
key_points: Marinate lamb chops in olive oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours | Rest chops out of the fridge 20–30 minutes before cooking for a crispier edge | Griddle on medium-high heat for 4 minutes each side, plus 30 seconds fat-side down | Boil the used marinade with water for 3–4 minutes to cook off bacteria, then pour over chops to serve

title: Baked Peaches & Brie Charcuterie Dip
one_liner: A summer charcuterie board baked into one bubbly, scoopable dip with peaches, Brie, and hot honey.
caption:
Been daydreaming about that Peaches & Brie Charcuterie Dip all week🤤🍑🧀

Sweet peaches, juicy blackberries, creamy Brie, crispy prosciutto, fresh thyme, and Aleppo hot honey baked until golden, bubbly, and perfect for scooping. It’s everything you love about a summer charcuterie board in one ridiculously good bite.🫠

Save this and send it to the friend who has to bring the wine. 🍷

Baked Peaches & Brie Charcuterie Dip 🍑🧀

2 ripe peaches, diced
1/2 cup blackberries
8 oz Brie, chopped
2 oz prosciutto, torn
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
Kosher salt & black pepper
Aleppo Hot Honey (Comment “yum” and I’ll DM you the recipe.)

Add everything to a baking dish, pour over the hot honey, and sprinkle over salt and pepper. 

Bake at 425°F  for 12-15  minutes, until the Brie is melted and bubbling.

Remove from the oven, and drizzle over balsamic drizzle.
 
Serve warm with garlic rubbed crostini, or your favorite crackers and enjoy!

key_points: Traumatic experiences cause the brain to build identity statements ('I'm broken', 'I'm too much') as survival interpretations, not facts. | Neurologically, these beliefs are just rehearsed neural pathways — they feel like identity but aren't permanent. | Metacognition (prefrontal cortex stepping back) lets you question who or what taught you those beliefs, loosening their grip. | Healing isn't becoming someone new — it's recognizing that trauma-built identities were survival code, not your true self.
transcript: Things I can say for free or therapists can't. Remember the spoon scene in the Matrix? The child tells Neo something strange. Do not try and bend the spoon. That's impossible. Instead, realize the truth. There is no spoon. The point was not that the spoon disappeared. It was that the spoon only existed inside the Matrix's cult. Once Neo understood that, he stopped trying to force the spoon to change. Instead, he changed how he understood the system. Trauma works the same way with identity. When something painful happens, the brain writes identity around it. I'm too much, I'm not enough, I'm difficult, or I'm broken. And over time, those things stop feeling like beliefs and start feeling like who you are. But neurologically, those identity statements are just rehearsed neural pathways. They're survival interpretations your brain built to make sense of pain. They're not permanent truths about your identity. And that is where metacognition comes in. Your prefrontal cortex stepping back and asking, who told me this about myself? Or what taught me this about myself? The moment you start questioning the identity code, the system starts losing its grip. Because the brain can't keep controlling you with the script you've already examined. Healing from trauma is not becoming someone new. It's realizing that some of the identities you've been carrying aren't truly you. They were survival code. And the moment you see that clearly, you stop bending yourself to try and fit the program and instead step outside of it. Because once you understand that the identity was written by the system, you realize something powerful. There was never a spoon defining you in the first place.

caption:
Please don’t come @ me with peppers being higher in vitamin C, we’re here for function AND flavor. 

My mother-in laws Preserved Lemons:

Ingredients (for 1 jar)
 • 1 lemon (or 2–4 if using a bigger jar)
 • coarse sea salt 
 • olive oil, enough to fully cover

 1. Take a clean glass jar (you can sterilize it once with boiling water and let it dry.)
 2. Wash the lemons and slice them into thin rounds. Clean hands.
 3. Start layering: lemon slices, a good pinch of salt, lemon, salt - keep going until everything is packed in.
 4. Press everything down firmly so the lemons start releasing their juice.
 5. Pour olive oil over the top until everything is completely covered. (the lemons should always stay under the oil.)
 6. Close the jar and keep it in a cool place.

They’ll be ready after about 3 days. Over time (1–2 weeks), they get more mellow and develop a deeper, slightly fermented flavor.

Use the peel and the flesh in salads, grains, roasted veg and the oil on top is honestly one of the best parts.

*feel free to play around with the flavor base. Try peppercorns, bay leaves, garlic or mustard seeds, and a little chili for heat. Just keep it balanced so the lemons stay the main character.

from anything

not by denying the harm

When you see clearly
that you were also loved.
That you also caused harm.
That you were also given to.

The story of being
only wronged
becomes impossible to sustain.

And the energy spent maintaining it
comes flooding back.

Clinical research
at Kyushu University found
that patients who completed Naikan

in depression

relationship quality.

Not because their relationships changed.

Because they did.

Don’t lose this page.

Clarity. Instinct. Flow.

They’re defeated by rehearsing fear every day.

Accept the loss for 60 seconds.

Marketing isn’t a strategy problem. It’s a mirror.

title: Mediterranean Eggplant Pocket Bake
one_liner: Roasted eggplant slices folded into pockets around spiced ground beef, baked in marinara and topped with mozzarella.
caption:
💥Mediterranean Eggplant Pocket Bake

If you love easy mediterranean meals, and want a healthy weeknight dinner, you’ve got to try this pocket bake - these come out so good, so saucy, so cheesy, and so easy to make. It’s one of those meals that feels a little extra… but is actually super straightforward.

Ingredients:
2-3 medium eggplants, sliced 1/4–1/3 inch thick
Olive oil
Salt

For the filling:
1lb 80/20 ground beef
1/3 yellow onion, finely diced
2 garlic cloves, minced
1/2 tbsp onion powder
1 tbsp granulated garlic
1/2 tbsp sweet paprika
1 tbsp fresh parsley
Salt & pepper
Optional (if not low carb): 1/2 cup uncooked rice

For assembly:
1/2 jar marinara or pasta sauce
Sliced or shredded mozzarella cheese
Chili flakes
Fresh basil
Shredded parmesan

Here’s how I made it:

1️⃣ Preheat oven to 425°F.

2️⃣ Slice 2-3 eggplants into 1/4 to 1/3 inch thick slices. Lay them out on an oven-safe tray without overlapping. Season with salt and drizzle with olive oil. You may need 2 trays.

3️⃣ Roast for 18–20 mins.

4️⃣ While that cooks, make your beef mixture. In a bowl, combine 1lb ground beef with diced onion, the spices above, salt, and pepper. Mix well. If using rice, add 1/2 cup uncooked rice here.

5️⃣ Form the mixture into 6-8 equal patties or balls.

6️⃣ Remove eggplant from the oven and let cool for about 1 min. Take one slice and lay it across your palm, then place another slice across it in an “X” shape.

7️⃣ Add one beef patty in the center, then fold each side over to create a pocket. Repeat for all.

8️⃣ In an oven-safe dish, spread about half a jar of marinara on the bottom. Place the eggplant pockets on top. Cover with a lid. Bake at 425°F for 22–24 mins.

9️⃣ Remove, top with mozzarella and chili flakes, then broil for 2–3 mins until melted and bubbly.

Serve as-is, or top with shredded parmesan, some basil, or pair with a side of rice or @kaizenfoodco high-protein rice to make it low carb and even more filling.

If you make it, be sure to tag me on SHREDHAPPENS!

ENJOY!

title: Why Unfinished Relationships Haunt Us
one_liner: The Zeigarnik Effect explains why incomplete relationships and ghosting linger in our minds longer than resolved ones.
caption:
Zeigarnik: The Zeigarnik Effect

Why do we often think more about the ones who got away than the ones we said goodbye to?
key_points: The brain holds unfinished tasks and relationships with greater mental intensity than completed ones | Waiters easily forget orders once paid — proof the brain releases 'closed' tasks instantly | Ghosting feels cruel because it denies the brain a psychological 'full stop' needed to move on | Writing an unsent letter to someone who haunts you can give your brain the closure it needs to let go
transcript: Why do we often think more about the ones who got away than the ones we said goodbye to? Why do we think about the friends that we were never meant to lose touch with? This is known as the Zygarnik effect. In the 1920s, the researcher Bloomer Zygarnik noticed that waiters will often remember every detail of an open order. Table 4 wants fish, table 9 changed their wine. But the moment the bill was paid, the order vanished from their memory completely. The task was done and so the brain let go. Zygarnik went back to her lab and she proved that the mind will hold on with greater intensity to the unfinished task over the completed one. But this isn't just true for jobs or essays you have to do, but our personal relationships as well. If you have unfinished business with some long-lost friend, you will think about them a lot, you will dream about them. If you feel as though a romantic partner was torn from you, that will hurt more than if you walked away from them. This is why ghosting can feel so cruel, because it doesn't just end a relationship, it denies the other person's brain the one thing it needs to move on, a full stop. The lesson here is that the brain doesn't need a happy ending, it just needs some kind of ending. And so if somebody still haunts your thoughts, then write them a letter or pen them a message. You might not send either, but doing so will gift your brain the full stop that it needs to let go.

one_liner: Playing by your own rules activates dopamine and agency, while following others wires your brain for mediocrity.
caption:
The people who change the world are usually the ones who were told they were “too much,” “too unrealistic,” or “doing life wrong.”

Your brain was not designed to find your purpose by copying everyone else.

The moment you stop blindly following the script you were handed, you stop living on autopilot.

key_points: Following others' rules trains repetitive survival loops, suppressing motivation and authenticity | Taking personal risks activates exploratory brain networks and boosts dopamine | Breaking from the expected strengthens the prefrontal cortex and disrupts autopilot (default mode network) | Perceived agency over your life is one of the strongest predictors of well-being

Playing it safe wires your brain for mediocrity. And it takes you out of your authenticity, which is where you are the most magnetic. But when you start playing by your own rules and taking risks, your brain shifts. You activate exploratory networks in your brain instead of repetitive survival loops, which boosts dopamine and motivation because you're actually choosing your path. You strengthen your prefrontal cortex so that you can actually be the boss of your own life. You also shake up the default mode network, which gets you out of autopilot and into being the creator of your life. Feeling like you have agency over your own life is one of the strongest predictors of well-being. And when you're following everyone else's rules, you don't have that. Creativity literally requires deviation from established patterns. That's why every visionary looks delusional before they look successful. author: AYO FURY
title: Chemical Engineer's Science-Backed Lemon Loaf
one_liner: A chemical engineer optimizes lemon loaf for intense citrus flavor using food science principles.
caption:
Lemon Loaf 🍋 🍞 // How a chemical engineer would make the World’s best lemon loaf. I tested this one 8 times and got an addicting, moist, and dense lemon loaf. I’ve optimized it for intense lemon flavor but has other flavors in the background making it way better than one you buy at the store.

Recipe
This recipe is for a 8x4 loaf. If your pan is 9x5, multiply all ingredient measurements by 1.5. 

Loaf 
165g granulated sugar
Zest of 1 lemon
Zest of 1 lime
Zest of 1 orange 
1 tsp grated fresh ginger
1 egg
75g olive oil
65g almond milk
145g AP flour 
1 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
30g lemon juice (1/2 lemon)
10g lime juice (1/2 lime)

Lemon Syrup
30g lemon juice
15g lime juice 
25g Powdered sugar

1. This recipe is for a 8x4 loaf. If you are using a 9x5 loaf, multiply ingredient measurements by 1.5.
2. Preheat oven to 160C/320F convection/fan setting. Otherwise use 180C/350F if you do not have fan setting. Grease and line your loaf tin with parchment paper.
3. In a large bowl, add sugar, all zests, and fresh ginger. Rub all of these together with your fingers until the sugar is resembles yellow damp sand. Let sit for 15 minutes to absorb all the essential oils
4. Add egg and olive oil. Whisk and let sit 5 minutes. A lot the sugar should be dissolved after 5 minutes.
5. Add milk and whisk. Make sure all sugar is dissolved.
6. Add dry ingredients, lemon juice, and lime juice at the same time and mix until well combined.
7. Pour batter into lined loaf tin. Bake for 55-60 minutes the loaf will be golden should spring back when you press the top.
8. Prepare lemon syrup by mixing everything together. 
9. Once loaf is out, let rest for 10 minutes, then poke holes throughout the loaf with a skinny skewer. 
10. Spoon lemon syrup over the hot loaf. Make sure to get the edges. It’ll soak up the syrup quickly.

Optional: A glaze - mix runny Greek yogurt, powdered sugar, lemon juice until combined and drizzle over the top once nearly cooled
Pro tip: once cooled, wrap tightly in plastic wrap over night. It will be super moist the next day.
key_points: Bake at 160°C instead of 180°C to prevent limonene and citral (citrus flavor molecules) from degrading | Add lime zest and juice alongside lemon — lime's pinene and terpene molecules add woody/spice background notes that make the flavor more complex | Rub sugar with zests and ginger for 15 minutes to extract essential oils before mixing the batter | Poke holes and soak the hot loaf with lemon-lime syrup immediately after baking for maximum moisture
transcript: This is how a chemical engineer makes the world's best lemon loaf. First, a chemical engineer would never bake at 180°C or 350°F. Citrus flavor comes from the flavor molecules limonene and citrile, which is thermally unstable. At 180°C, these are already beginning to degrade and evaporate off the loaf. That's why most loaves never really taste like lemon. So a chemical engineer would bake at 160°C to reduce some of the citrus degradation. Now lemon by itself can be a bit boring and even taste like soap. So to put it this way, you would never wear just a pure lemon cologne or perfume, right? It has to have like wood or floral notes in the background. Otherwise, it just smells like cleaning chemicals. The same concept applies to lemon loaf. In addition to limonene and citrile, lime contains pinyin and terpene, which are green wood and spice molecules found in pine trees, oregano, and thyme. Adding a little lime to your lemon syrup gives a background flavor to the lemon loaf and makes it far more satisfying to eat, but no one will know your secret. Wow. All because of science.

transcript: I made $100K in a month without asking people to buy my shit. And no, I did not use reverse sales psychology or sales tactics. I just learned how ATMs work. Let me explain. Both extremes are f***ing you over. So let me show you how to fix that. I stopped thinking about content as value posts versus sales posts and started thinking about it like a bank account. Imagine you're at an ATM in the US. You deposit US dollars. The machine reads that you can withdraw it later. It works. But what if you started depositing Japanese Yen, Euros, Monopoly money? They might have value somewhere, but this ATM can't read it, so it spits it back out. Yes, you made a deposit, but it doesn't count. That's what most of you are doing with your content. You're making the deposits, but it's in the wrong currency. You're posting tips that sound good, but doesn't really get anyone results. So when you finally ask for the sale, your account stays empty. So the question here is, what is the right currency and what deposits actually count? First is value that gets results, not tips or inspirational posts. These are actionable and tangible steps that people can start implementing today and actually see a change. The wrong currency looks like, here's 10 tips to lose weight. Number one, progressive overload. Number two, eat more protein. Number three, eat your veggies. That doesn't do anything, okay? Those are deposits that count. And that is a currency this ATM accepts. Now, how many times should you be posting before you make a sale? Here's my rule. 90% of the time, give so much value, and then 10% do an ask. Not talent, not circumstances, not even the quality of your decisions-but how quickly you collapse the space between intention and reality. Think of this gap as a kind of friction coefficient on your existence: the smaller it is, the more of your internal force actually translates into external motion. When you can move from “I should do this” to physically doing it within hours instead of weeks, you’re not just accomplishing more-you’re operating in a fundamentally different mode of being where your thoughts have immediate consequences in the world, where your inner life and outer life are in a constant, tight, conversation.

title: Crispy Lentil Crackers: No Oil, All Crunch
one_liner: Make high-protein, high-fiber lentil crackers using just lentils, water, and spices — no oil needed.
caption:
Crispy, high protein, high fiber crackers — no frying, no oil.
By @wendythefoodscientist

Just lentils, water and spices. That's it.
Here's the food science behind why it works: when soaked lentils are blended, their starches gelatinize in the oven and then dehydrate — forming a thin, glassy crunch. No oil needed. The crispiness comes from the starch, not the fat.
Spread thin, bake twice, and you get a snap that sounds like a proper cracker.
Use any lentil, any seeds, any spices. New batch every week.

Ingredients
125g / ⅔ cup dry lentils
100ml / ⅓ cup + 1 tbsp water
30g / 3 tbsp sesame seeds
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp dried rosemary

Method
Soak lentils in cold water for 8-12 hours. Drain and rinse well.
Add soaked lentils and water to a high-speed blender. Blend until completely smooth — no lumps remaining.
Add sesame seeds, salt and rosemary. Stir to combine.
Spread as thinly as possible onto a lined baking tray.
Bake at 180°C / 355°F for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven and cut into squares or rectangles.
Return to oven and bake for a further 30-35 minutes until golden, dry and crispy.
Allow to cool completely before serving — they crisp up further as they cool.

author: Wendy the Food Scientist
title: Soak Nuts for the Crispiest Granola Ever
one_liner: Soaking nuts and seeds before baking removes bitter tannins and creates a crispier, more porous granola texture.
caption:
Why soak your nuts and seeds for the best granola ever
By @wendythefoodscientist

I’ve been doing this for a long time but rarely see it shared online, so here’s my secret: soaking nuts and seeds before making granola.
Why?
1. Cleaner flavor: Soaking + rinsing leaches some bitter tannins (especially in walnuts/sunflower seed), so the nutty taste is smooth and clean.
2. Crispier bite: Soaking improves texture because the nuts and seeds swell, and after drying it is more brittle, more porous. The result is super crispy.
When to use it?
For granola, roasted nuts, or any other recipe where you want extra crispy and tasty nuts/seeds
How to soak?
Rule of thumb
- Almonds: 8–12 h
- Walnuts, pecan, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds: 4–6 h
- Cashews: 2–4 h
- Sesame seeds: optional, 1-2 h
Rinse, soak in salted water (1.5-2 tsp per L), rinse again

The nutritional benefits of “activated” nuts are debated. While soaking may reduce some antinutrients, the enzymes activated during soaking don’t survive high-heat baking. If enzyme activity matters to you, dehydrate at low temperatures ≤50–60°C (122-140°F) instead.
The reason I soak is for texture and flavor. This method delivers the crispiest, most delicious granola I’ve ever made. I have developed a method that can be done with any oven.

Bake soaked nuts and seeds 130°C / 265°F 30-40min until dry and lightly toasted
175°C / 350°F 15-20min until roasted.

#healthyfood #healthyeating #cookinghack

transcript: This is my secret to the best granola you've ever tasted. Perfectly crispy and tasty in 5 simple steps. Rinse your nuts and seeds then soak them to draw out soluble bitter compounds like tannins. After soaking, rinse again to wash away what's been released. Then bake at low temperature until dry to the touch. Lastly, add the rest of the granola ingredients and bake until golden. It gets even crispier as it cools when you can hear it crackling in the pan. Most recipes skip the soaking step but trust me, this is what takes your granola to the next level.

title: High-Protein Blueberry Cheesecake
one_liner: A 6-ingredient baked blueberry cheesecake using cottage cheese for extra protein.
caption:
Healthy High Protein Blueberry Cheesecake 🍰😋🫐 

Ingredients: 
3 tbsp cottage cheese
2 oz cream cheese
1 large egg
2 tbsp sweetener (I used monkfruit)
2 tbsp blueberries
1 tsp vanilla extract

Instructions:
1. Blend all ingredients except the blueberries and pour it in a greased dish.
2. Add your blueberries & bake @ 325F for 30-35 mins. 
3. Take it out, chill for a couple hours & enjoy!

Pro tip: Mash some extra blueberries and swirl them in the top with a toothpick👌
